transcript.note: Deliberately independent method from llm-skeleton2grid (which used rank-order coarsening): here col=round(gx/77), row=round((1000-gy)/77), i.e. actual proportional geographic distance rather than rank, so real gaps (e.g. the 317-unit jump from 10 to 12, the 181-unit jump from 14 to 10) stay as real column spacing instead of being collapsed to adjacent integers. This intentionally keeps far-apart stations visually far apart (lower meanDrift potential) at the cost of fewer H/V hits than a rank-collapsed grid, since real gx/gy rarely line up exactly -- that tradeoff is exactly what this ablation (no rank-snapping baseline to lean on) is supposed to expose. After the base proportional pass (hv=9/20), moved stations 10 and 12 from row3 to row4 to join the row that 8/13/16 already proportionally rounded to (checked pairwise against all 17 points that this does not flip any geographic order, only ties broken in the exempt way), which turns 16-10 into a third horizontal segment of the orange-line trunk without disturbing 10-12's existing alignment. All 5 interchanges (3,4,7,8,16) checked by hand: 360-degree neighbour order matches geography. No collisions, no vertex sits on another edge's straight segment.

Round 2: moved station 9 (deg 2, so no winding-order check applies at it or at its neighbours 1/5, both deg<=2) from row9 to row8, matching station 5's row. Verified pairwise against all 15 other points that no geographic order flips. Turns edge 9-5 into a clean horizontal segment (no vertex sits between col3 and col5 at row8), raising hv from 10 to 11. Edge 1-9 stays diagonal either way (1's column/row are pinned by nothing else nearby to merge into safely).
